t: Section 4712(a) of title 10, United States Code, is amended by striking out “the court-martial jurisdiction of the Army or the Air Force” and inserting in place thereof “military law”.

fable.w: This is a purely technical amendment substituting one phrase for another in 10 U.S.C. 4712(a). The tempting reading is that the word "jurisdiction" signals a litigation right or hearing, but it only describes which persons are subject to military law and gives no outside party a right to sue or object. There is no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, or rulemaking involving anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: is amended by striking out “the court-martial jurisdiction of the Army or the Air Force” and inserting in place thereof “military law”

The text describes a change in statutory language regarding military law, not a mechanism for outside participation in government decision-making.
qwen_block.s: Section 4712(a) of title 10, United States Code, is amended by striking out “the court-martial jurisdiction of the Army or the Air Force” and inserting in place thereof “military law”.

opus.w: This is a technical amendment that only changes the wording of a jurisdictional reference in Title 10. No one outside the federal government is consulted, invited to comment or given a right to object before a federal decision. The mention of court-martial jurisdiction is not participation, because describing jurisdiction is not the same as giving an outside party a right to sue.

It does not create any mechanism for consultation, coordination, or participation by parties outside the federal government. The change is purely internal to the definition of legal authority within the military structure.
